detailed_summary: This paper constructs new Hermitian self-dual maximum-distance-separable (MDS) codes with parameters [12,6,7] over GF(25), [18,9,10] over GF(121), and [18,9,10] over GF(169). These codes are used to construct absolutely maximally entangled (AME) states of 12 parties with local dimension 5 (AME(12,5)), 18 parties with local dimension 11 (AME(18,11)), and 18 parties with local dimension 13 (AME(18,13)). Additionally, by projecting one party, the authors obtain AME(17,11) and AME(17,13) states. The [12,6,7]_{25} code is notable because it is not monomially equivalent to a generalized Reed-Solomon code, and it was found via a systematic search without any prescribed coordinate symmetry. The paper details a sophisticated search methodology that leverages group actions, group algebra decompositions, and exact field arithmetic to reduce the search space and certify the results. The authors also perform extensive verification, including complete enumeration of square minors and graph-state cut-rank computations.
key_contributions: Construction of new Hermitian self-dual MDS codes with parameters [12,6,7]_{25}, [18,9,10]_{121}, and [18,9,10]_{169}.
Derivation of new AME states: AME(12,5), AME(18,11), AME(18,13), and via projection AME(17,11) and AME(17,13).
Discovery of a [12,6,7]_{25} code that is not monomially equivalent to a generalized Reed-Solomon code, demonstrating the existence of non-GRS Hermitian self-dual MDS codes.
Development of an efficient search algorithm that uses group actions and group algebra decompositions to reduce the search space, enabling the discovery of length-18 codes.
Rigorous certification of Hermitian self-duality and MDS property via exact field arithmetic and complete square-minor enumeration, along with independent graph-state cut-rank checks.
methodology_analysis: The methodology combines algebraic construction, computational search, and rigorous verification. For the [12,6,7]_{25} code, a systematic search was performed without imposing coordinate symmetry, likely using a backtracking or randomized algorithm over the finite field GF(25). For the length-18 codes, the authors imposed a regular Z_3^2 action on two nine-coordinate orbits, which reduced the problem to finding a kernel in a nine-element group algebra. The Hermitian character decomposition of this group algebra splits the self-duality constraints into independent blocks, allowing exact family counts. A norm-one coordinate scaling was used to remove a factor of q+1=14 at q=13, further simplifying the search. The codes were certified by checking all square minors (for the MDS property) and verifying Hermitian self-duality using exact arithmetic. Additionally, graph-state cut-rank computations, including all single-vertex deletions, provided independent verification of the AME property.
results_analysis: The paper reports the explicit construction of three new Hermitian self-dual MDS codes, leading to new AME states. The [12,6,7]_{25} code is particularly significant as it is the first example of a Hermitian self-dual MDS code that is not monomially equivalent to a GRS code, challenging previous assumptions. The length-18 codes yield AME(18,11) and AME(18,13), which are new additions to the known set of AME states. The projection method yields AME(17,11) and AME(17,13), which are also new. The paper provides exact counts of families for the length-18 codes, and the removal of the q+1 factor at q=13 is a clever optimization. The verification is exhaustive, ensuring the results are correct.
strengths: The paper presents genuinely new results, including the first non-GRS Hermitian self-dual MDS code, which is a significant theoretical advance.
The computational methods are sophisticated and efficient, demonstrating the power of combining group theory with exact arithmetic to solve a hard search problem.
The verification is rigorous, with complete enumeration of square minors and independent graph-state cut-rank checks, leaving no room for error.
The paper is well-structured and provides sufficient detail for reproducibility, including the group algebra decomposition and scaling tricks.
limitations: The paper does not provide explicit generator matrices or the actual code constructions in the abstract; the full details are likely in the main text, but the abstract alone is insufficient for immediate use.
The search methods, while efficient, may not scale to larger lengths or dimensions without further innovations, as the search space grows rapidly.
The paper does not discuss the potential applications of these AME states in quantum error correction or other quantum information tasks, which could be of interest to a broader audience.
connections_to_research: This work directly relates to quantum physics, specifically to the study of absolutely maximally entangled states, which are crucial for quantum error correction, quantum secret sharing, and holographic quantum gravity. The construction of AME states via quantum error-correcting codes (specifically Hermitian self-dual MDS codes) is a central topic in quantum information theory. The new AME states, particularly AME(12,5) and AME(18,11), fill gaps in the known existence of AME states and may have implications for the classification of entanglement and the study of holographic codes. The paper's methods also connect to algebraic coding theory and finite geometry, which are foundational to quantum error correction.
overall_assessment: This is a high-quality paper that makes significant contributions to both quantum information theory and classical coding theory. The construction of new Hermitian self-dual MDS codes, especially the non-GRS example, is a major theoretical breakthrough. The computational techniques are innovative and well-executed, and the verification is thorough. The results are likely to stimulate further research into the existence and classification of AME states and self-dual MDS codes. The paper is well-written and the findings are presented with clarity. Overall, this is an important contribution that will be of interest to researchers in quantum physics, quantum information, and coding theory.
